Assertion (A): Executable files with extensions such as .exe, .bat, or .vbs are usually blocked by enterprise mail gateways. Reason (R): Executable file attachments represent a primary vector for malware propagation and unauthorized code execution.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (a). Enterprise email gateways automatically block incoming and outgoing file attachments containing executable script extensions to maintain perimeter security. Executable files can contain compiled binary instructions or automated script routines that execute malicious payloads upon opening. Restricting executable attachments reduces virus propagation, ransomware infections, and unauthorized code execution risks, safeguarding internal network workstations and centralized server infrastructure from compromise.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। एंटरप्राइज ईमेल गेटवे स्वचालित रूप से ऐसे फ़ाइल अटैचमेंट को ब्लॉक करते हैं जिनमें निष्पादन योग्य स्क्रिप्ट एक्सटेंशन होते हैं ताकि परिधीय सुरक्षा बनाए रखी जा सके। निष्पादन योग्य फ़ाइलों में संकलित बाइनरी निर्देश या स्वचालित स्क्रिप्ट रूटीन हो सकते हैं जो खोलने पर दुर्भावनापूर्ण पेलोड निष्पादित करते हैं। निष्पादन योग्य अटैचमेंट को प्रतिबंधित करने से वायरस प्रसार, रैनसमवेयर संक्रमण और अनधिकृत कोड निष्पादन के जोखिम कम होते हैं, जिससे आंतरिक नेटवर्क वर्कस्टेशनों और केंद्रीकृत सर्वर अवसंरचना को समझौता से सुरक्षित रखा जा सके।
key_facts: Executable files can contain harmful scripts that may compromise security.
Enterprise email gateways block executable attachments to prevent malware.
Restricting executable attachments reduces risks of virus propagation.
Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_english: Which policy governs the ownership and acceptable usage bounds of official institutional email accounts provided to employees?
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is the Acceptable Use Policy (AUP). An Acceptable Use Policy is an administrative security framework that establishes rules governing employee usage of institutional IT infrastructure, computing assets, and email accounts. The policy defines ownership boundaries, acceptable operational conduct, security compliance requirements, and prohibited activities. Enforcing these guidelines ensures regulatory compliance, safeguards institutional digital assets against misuse, and establishes legal accountability for system users across the organization.
